result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): The screenshots show only the top of each page. Both quizzes look alike and plausible, with no invented regulatory figures, so the scores for submit handling, the results view and the later questions are estimates. A edges ahead on layout: its questions sit in clean cards with clickable option rows, while B's wrapped question 2 heading runs awkwardly into the box border. A's load-limit question also adds a useful point that capacity drops as the load center moves farther out. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both screenshots show only the top of a plain five-question forklift quiz. The questions are similar and use no invented regulatory figures, and neither screenshot shows the submit button or results, so rubric items 1, 2 and 5 are partly scored on what the visible part suggests. B has a slight edge on presentation: its question cards are clean and the answer options are easy to click, while in A the long question 2 text wraps across the box border and looks awkward.
